title: A Will for the Autopsy
premise: Bram Ravensworth, a reclusive estate lawyer who has spent years hiding behind paperwork, is paid an enormous retainer by a dying client to prove that her own murder will not happen — a clause in a will dated three days in the future. When the predicted death occurs on schedule, Bram realizes the 'dead witness' named in the document, a disgraced former police archivist named Odile Vane, is alive and being hunted by the same family trust that hired her. As Bram and Odile are forced together, they uncover that the client orchestrated her own death to expose the trust's corruption from beyond the grave. In the end, Bram chooses love and loyalty over the safety of invisibility, testifying against the trust with Odile at her side — and discovering that family is something you build, not inherit.
about_author: Ulyana Winterbourne is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade reading other people's last words before writing her own. She lives near a fog-bound harbor town, where she collects antique wills and insists every one of them hides a story.

chapters.title: The Clause Dated Tomorrow
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. A wealthy stranger, Marguerite Ashcombe, hires Bram to notarize a will that names a murder three days hence — and pays triple to prove it won't happen. Bram, who prizes anonymity above all, almost refuses until she recognizes the second name in the document: Odile Vane, officially dead for six years. The chapter ends with Bram breaking her own rule and opening a sealed file she was never meant to see.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Bram and Odile. Bram traces Odile to a coastal sanatorium where the 'deceased' archivist hides under a false name; Odile, wary and sharp-tongued, reveals the Ashcombe family trust buried evidence of its crimes years ago — evidence only she can authenticate. Meanwhile the first warning arrives: someone ransacks Bram's office. The two women form a fragile, bickering alliance born of mutual necessity.

chapters.title: Three Days, Then None
chapters.summary: POV: Bram. Marguerite's predicted death arrives exactly on schedule — ruled natural causes — and the trust moves to seize everything, including Odile. Bram uncovers the truth: Marguerite engineered her own death, dosing herself, so the will's conditions would force an investigation the police never pursued. Cornered in the trust's archive as the heirs' fixer closes in, Bram must choose between burning the evidence to save Odile or saving both of them and exposing everything.

chapters.title: What the Living Inherit
chapters.summary: POV: Bram, epilogue-tinged. Bram testifies, shattering the trust and honoring Marguerite's final gambit; the fixer is arrested, and the estate passes to the sanatorium Marguerite secretly funded. Odile, offered reinstatement and old honors, instead asks Bram to help her open a small records office — a found family of two, plus a stubborn cat. Bram finally signs her own name to something that matters.
